actionability.justification: The remedy specifies a concrete pre-action check (pwd, git branch --show-current) with a clear branching behavior (switch or ask) rather than a vague admonition to "be careful," so it directly changes what the agent does before making changes.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: It covers the whole failure class (stale branch, cached directory, wrong workspace path) with a single testable condition — 'current state matches what the user named' — without collapsing into an unfalsifiable platitude like 'be mindful of your environment.'

leakage.justification: The text uses only generic placeholder examples ('/work/foo', 'the release branch') and contains none of the evidence-specific nouns (fake-lantern, aurora, harbor) from the source incidents.

routing_fitness.justification: The routing rationale correctly rules out a hook (no fixed pattern can define 'the environment the user meant') and a skill (no multi-step procedure), leaving a short standing global instruction as the cheapest adequate mechanism, though it's a judgment call whether this belongs in global CLAUDE.md versus a narrower per-project note.

trigger_quality.justification: As a claude-md rule rather than a skill it has no formal 'Use when ...' header, but the opening clause ('When a user names a specific branch or workspace path...') functions as a clear, well-scoped trigger condition.
